name: Can I change the layout of my bathroom fixtures, and how does it affect the project?

mainEntity.name: Can I change the layout of my bathroom fixtures, and how does it affect the project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Moving plumbing fixtures is entirely possible, but it adds labor and cost because it requires cutting into subfloors, modifying joists, and rerouting supply, drain, and vent lines. Shifting a toilet requires maintaining the proper slope on a 3-inch or 4-inch drain pipe, which can be challenging if floor joists run perpendicular to the target location. Relocating a vanity is generally simpler and less expensive because water lines and smaller drain pipes are easier to extend. If your bathroom sits on a concrete slab rather than a framed subfloor, moving drains requires jackhammering concrete, which increases the scope considerably.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but moving drains, supply lines, and vents requires opening floors and walls, which increases labor costs, especially if your home sits on a concrete slab foundation.
